text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The government has sent to parliament the draft first year of the fourth five-year plan and the draft budget for the next financial year beginning July 1. The budget contains three allowances for public-sector workers to be paid from July.

- President Hosni Mubarak will make a comprehensive political speech on the occasion of Labour Day celebrations organised by the Trade Union Federation tomorrow. His speech will cover developments at home and abroad and the role of workers in the coming stage.
- Sheikh Khalifa bin Zaid Al Nahayan, the crown prince of Abu Dhabi, arrives in Cairo today on a two-day official visit at the invitation of Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri.

- Agriculture Minister Youssef Wali said starting July an agricultural development strategy for the period up to 2017 will start. It includes reclamation of 2.65 million acres (1.07 million hectares) at a rate of 150,000 acres a year.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa begins an African tour today covering Djibouti, Tanzania, Kenya and Uganda. He will deliver letters to the heads of state from President Hosni Mubarak.

- Total deposits in Egyptian banks other than the Central Bank amounted to 154.251 billion pounds ($45.44 billion) at the end of January this year, against 136.461 billion one year earlier, the Central Bank's latest report said.
- Sudanese security broke into the resthouse used by workers for an Egyptian contracting company in Khartoum without reason. They searched all the contents in a provocative manner.
- Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said that peace was at a dead end because of the obstinacy of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
- The ministry of manpower announced that Thursday May 1 will be a paid holiday.

- The Grand Sheikh of al-Azhar, Mohamed Sayyed Tantawi, has decided to abolish all the fatwa committees in the Azhar educational areas in the provinces with effect from July 1. The employees will become Koran recitation teachers. He said the aim was to give the imams of mosques a chance to fulfil their role in guiding people to the True Religion.
- Informed sources in Damascus expect that Mubarak and Syrian President Hafez al-Assad will hold a summit in Cairo tomorrow or at the beginning of next week.
